source_documents.title: Dual-Excited-State Intramolecular Proton Transfer Pathways Observed in Fisetin

reference_evidence_units.quote: Meanwhile, the green fluorescence band with a large Stokes shift is attributed to the emission from the T* generated via the ESIPT process.
reference_evidence_units.subject: fisetin
reference_evidence_units.statement: Weak N* emission (~400-430 nm) and strong T* emission (~540 nm) with a Stokes shift above 9900 cm-1.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Steady-state assignment follows earlier literature on 3-hydroxyflavones.

reference_evidence_units.quote: pathways were directly observed when fisetin was dissolved in acetone and acetonitrile.
reference_evidence_units.subject: fisetin
reference_evidence_units.statement: Femtosecond TA resolves ESIPT from both N*-S1 and N*-S2.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Pathway proportions come from global fitting of a kinetic model.

reference_evidence_units.quote: This is direct evidence for the occurrence of the N*-S1 → N*-S2 population transfer in fisetin even if only the N*-S1 state is excited.
reference_evidence_units.subject: fisetin
reference_evidence_units.statement: TRIR marker bands show S1→S2 population transfer before ESIPT.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Band assignment relies on TD-DFT frequencies.

reference_evidence_units.quote: the lowest energies of the N*-S1 and N*-S2 states of fisetin also present a degenerate trend, with an energy gap of only 0.13 eV
reference_evidence_units.subject: fisetin
reference_evidence_units.limitations: Single functional; vibrational-mode argument is labelled speculative by the authors.
